chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I brought a letter to my father; a man had given it to me, so I took it out from my sleeve. He said, 'O my son, do not carry anything in your sleeve, for the sleeve is a place of loss.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of carrying items in the sleeve in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises his son against carrying items in his sleeve (*kumm*), identifying it as a 'place of loss' (*mudya'*) due to its tendency to be overlooked or forgotten. This practical guidance underscores the Shia emphasis on *hifz al-amana* (preservation of trust) and mindfulness in daily transactions, linking physical care of belongings to broader ethical responsibility.
